lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.unitTitle: Kitchen Care and Basic Food Safety
lessonRef.title: Correction and reflection: storage and cleanup

objective: Using a specific instance of food or kitchen items not stored or cleaned up correctly, learners diagnose the break with an adult and correct both the immediate problem and their storage/cleanup routine.
scenario: The learner looks at a real, current kitchen storage or cleanup problem — leftovers left on the counter, a container put in the wrong cabinet, a dirty surface — and works with an adult to trace back exactly where the storage-and-cleanup routine broke down, then fixes it and adjusts the routine.
safetyNotes: No shame language is used toward whoever is responsible for the lapse.

simulationAlternative.description: If there's no current real storage or cleanup problem to diagnose, the learner instead reviews a short written kitchen-storage scenario, identifies the likely sticking-point step, and proposes a specific fix the same way as the guided task.

materials: the actual current kitchen item(s) needing correction

tasks.directions: Describe the specific storage or cleanup problem you're looking at right now — exactly what's out of place or left undone.
With your adult, trace back to the exact step where the routine stopped (food not covered, container not labeled, surface not wiped, etc.).

prompts.text: I named the exact step where the routine stopped.
My adult and I agreed on one specific reason that step was skipped.
We named one small change to make that step easier to remember.

tasks.directions: Correct the current problem, then test your one routine change on a second, similar situation.

prompts.text: Did the change work the second time? What did you notice?
Explain your updated storage-and-cleanup routine in your own words, and name the one step you'll watch most closely next time.

remediation: If the learner's proposed fix is vague, reteach by having them name a specific trigger (a location, a time, a linked habit) tied to the sticking-point step, then test it on a small, low-stakes situation before applying it to the real problem.
extension: Check one additional kitchen storage or cleanup habit for the same kind of breakdown and compare whether it's the same sticking-point step.
